title: Palmyrene Empire
capsule: The Palmyrene Empire was a breakaway state of the Roman Empire centered on the desert metropolis of Palmyra (Tadmor) in Syria, existing from roughly 260 to 273 CE. It emerged when the Palmyrene general Odaenathus exploited the crisis following Emperor Valerian's capture by the Sasanians in 260, defeating Shapur I's forces and assuming titles as 'King of Kings' and Corrector of the East before his assassination in 267. His widow Zenobia then governed as regent for their son Vaballathus, conquering Egypt, much of Asia Minor, and the Levant by 271 and briefly declaring herself Augusta. Emperor Aurelian counterattacked in 272, defeated Zenobia's forces near Immae and then at Emesa, and captured her fleeing toward the Euphrates; he razed Palmyra after a subsequent revolt in 273, ending the state entirely.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Palmyrene Empire's core territory in Syria and the Levant is well-attested by numismatic and epigraphic evidence; the precise extent of its control in Asia Minor and Egypt at any given month is less certain and depends on interpretation of fragmentary papyrological sources.
